purpose: Bounded GAO-26-107473 route from disability disclosure and workforce-program access through service use and post-exit employment/earnings comparisons, preserving accommodation, completion, remedy, and retention gaps.

events.geography: United States DOL workforce programs; selected state/local agencies and 12 visited job centers
events.date_precision: GAO report published January 21, 2026; participant data July 2023–June 2024 and recommendation status updated July 2026
events.denominator: Selected DOL workforce-program participants; 7% reported a disability, 43% of those did not report disability type; outcome bases vary by program and quarter
events.method: GAO participant-data analysis, interviews, document review, selected visits to 12 job centers, and review of DOL monitoring and guidance
events.missingness: Accommodation request/receipt, wait time, functional need, service completion, placement, hours, wages, retention, benefit transition, complaint, and participant-reported experience are not linked in the retained record
events.exposure: People reporting disabilities entered selected workforce-program records; GAO also reports more than 500,000 people with disabilities were unemployed and actively seeking work in each year from 2021 through 2024
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative job centers, training providers, transportation, informal support, disclosure choices, and non-program routes are not observed for the same participant
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Selected local officials reported challenges providing sign-language interpreters and accessible outside training; assistive technology availability was reported but successful use was not verified
events.choice_or_response: Participants reporting disabilities had lower post-exit employment and median second-quarter earnings in each core program; Adult training-service use was 33% versus 47% among participants reporting no disability
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Job centers, training providers, state agencies, and DOL control parts of the route; participants control disclosure and may request accommodation, but individual authority and choice conditions are not retained
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: DOL monitoring and three GAO recommendations are visible; DOL did not routinely aggregate monitoring reports, and recommendation implementation was not shown to improve participant outcomes
events.immediate_outcome: The record connects formal workforce-program access inputs to a measured post-exit employment/earnings comparison while leaving conversion mechanisms unresolved
events.protected_outcome: Accessible services could protect labor-market entry and earnings opportunity, but completion, placement, and durable retention are not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Access barriers, non-disclosure, lower training use, or local implementation gaps may sacrifice time and employment opportunity, but individual sacrifice is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The record does not identify whether accommodation, transport, technology, or failed-service costs transfer to participants, providers, employers, or public agencies
events.later_outcome: No same-participant job retention, wage trajectory, household security, benefit transition, trust, political action, or exit is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: Non-disclosure may protect privacy or reflect distrust, but the record does not identify participant interpretation, dignity, fairness, or blame
events.public_or_collective_response: Oversight and recommendations are observed; participant complaint, organizing, collective action, and later institutional response are not linked
events.counterexample: Lower outcomes may reflect disability type, prior work history, local labor demand, service mix, selection, or voluntary non-disclosure rather than inaccessible services alone
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO participant comparison and selected implementation review; sites are non-generalizable, disability status is reported, and the outcome gap is not a causal estimate

arrows.evidence: GAO reports lower employment rates and median second-quarter earnings for participants reporting disabilities in each core program; Adult second-quarter employment was 60% versus 76% and median earnings $7,048 versus $8,872
arrows.counterexample: Disability type, severity, prior work, local demand, selection, and service mix may explain the gap; the comparison is not causal
arrows.remaining_gap: Accommodation, service completion, placement, hours, wage rate, retention, and same-participant follow-up

arrows.evidence: In the Adult program, 33% of participants reporting disabilities used training services versus 47% of participants reporting no disability
arrows.counterexample: Service selection may reflect participant goals, disability type, prior training, provider availability, or disclosure rather than access failure
arrows.remaining_gap: Requested service, accommodation, wait, completion, credential, provider, and reason for non-use

arrows.evidence: GAO's selected visits found reported interpreter and outside-training accessibility challenges, while DOL did not routinely aggregate local monitoring reports
arrows.counterexample: The 12 visited centers were selected for variation and are not representative; local staff may resolve barriers that are not visible in aggregate monitoring
arrows.remaining_gap: Comparable site measures, participant encounter records, correction, and later service completion

arrows.to: durable placement, retention, earnings, and household security
arrows.evidence: The report has post-exit employment and earnings comparisons but does not link accommodation, completion, placement, retention, or household outcomes for the same participant
arrows.counterexample: A participant can complete a service and still face local labor demand or health constraints; employment at one quarter is not durable security
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-participant route from accommodation and completion through placement, hours, wages, retention, benefits, and recovery

arrows.to: correction, trust, voice, political action, or exit
arrows.evidence: GAO records recommendations and an oversight aggregation gap but no participant-level correction, complaint resolution, trust, organizing, or exit outcome
arrows.counterexample: A formal recommendation may change agency practice without improving a participant's usable route; non-disclosure or non-use may be privacy protection rather than withdrawal
arrows.remaining_gap: Participant-reported experience, complaint/appeal, agency correction, later trust, repeat use, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes a disability-access and workforce-program implementation stage beneath formal eligibility and above employment outcomes. It does not establish causal accommodation effects, service abandonment, placement, durable retention, household recovery, trust, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only GAO-published aggregate comparisons, selected implementation findings, recommendation status, and interpretation limits are retained; DOL participant files and local job-center records are not stored.
